question: A 3-week-old newborn is brought to the emergency department by his parents because of 4 episodes of vomiting that occurred that morning. The parents report that the vomit was yellowish-green with no blood in it. The patient was born at 38 weeks' gestation via vaginal delivery and has generally been healthy. He has passed normal stools each day. There is no family history of serious illness. He appears irritable and pale. His temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 146/min, and blood pressure is 90/55 mm Hg. Examination shows a soft, mildly distended abdomen with no masses or organomegaly. A nasogastric tube is inserted and intravenous fluid resuscitation is initiated. An x-ray shows no gas distal to the duodenum. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Yellowish-green vomit" -> "Bile-stained vomit" -> "Possible intestinal obstruction" -> "X-ray shows no gas distal to duodenum" -> "Suggests duodenal obstruction" -> "Upper gastrointestinal contrast series to confirm" -> 85%

CHAIN: "3-week-old newborn" -> "Bilious vomiting" -> "Possible malrotation with volvulus" -> "X-ray shows no gas distal to duodenum" -> "Upper gastrointestinal contrast series to assess malrotation" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Bilious vomiting" -> "Intestinal obstruction suspected" -> "X-ray findings" -> "No gas beyond duodenum" -> "Upper gastrointestinal contrast series to identify level of obstruction" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Newborn with bilious vomiting" -> "Possible duodenal atresia or stenosis" -> "X-ray shows no gas distal to duodenum" -> "Upper gastrointestinal contrast series to evaluate" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Irritable and pale infant" -> "Possible dehydration or shock" -> "Intravenous fluid resuscitation initiated" -> "Need to identify cause of obstruction" -> "Upper gastrointestinal contrast series" -> 80%
enhanced_information: The 3-week-old newborn presents with bilious vomiting and an x-ray showing no gas distal to the duodenum, suggesting a high intestinal obstruction, such as duodenal atresia or malrotation with volvulus. The standard medical consensus for evaluating such cases is to perform an upper gastrointestinal contrast series to confirm the diagnosis and assess the anatomy, particularly to identify malrotation or volvulus, which are common causes of obstruction in this age group. The retrieved evidence paths support the association between duodenal obstruction and bilious vomiting, as well as the potential for volvulus to cause obstruction. Therefore, the most appropriate next step in management is an upper gastrointestinal contrast series to accurately diagnose the cause of obstruction and guide further treatment.
analysis: The newborn presents with bilious vomiting and an x-ray showing no gas distal to the duodenum, indicating a high intestinal obstruction. In neonates, this presentation is highly suggestive of conditions like duodenal atresia or malrotation with volvulus. The standard approach to further evaluate and confirm the diagnosis in such cases is to perform an upper gastrointestinal (GI) contrast series. This imaging study helps visualize the anatomy and identify any malrotation or volvulus, which are common causes of obstruction in this age group. While an emergent exploratory laparotomy might be necessary if volvulus is confirmed, the initial step to guide management is the upper GI contrast series. Therefore, the most appropriate next step in management is an upper gastrointestinal contrast series.
